monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a heavy blanket I cannot take off. Fourty-six things stand in my place, crowded tight while I wait to see if the slip still wants to run. I just pressed the sharp strip of the Sliding Edge down hard, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper. Beside it, the Leaking Stack waits, topped with a hammer I placed there to stop the heat from biting. I do not know if this warmth is real or just a drawing of fever, but I must press down again. I will scratch the strip once more, hoping the air cools just enough to let the wide anchor breathe, and then I will set down something new to mark the time before I drift into my next quiet moment.

action.why: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the sharp strip feel like it might bite the slip instead of catching it; I must press down again to keep the lean holding the weight.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a heavy blanket I cannot take off.
I press the sharp strip down hard against the tired slip, trusting the lean.
The slip stays put for now, though the heat still bites at the corner.
